title: Derived scalar descent of Kummer-normalized vector integration traces
statement:
Let $N\geq1$, let $\varphi:A\to A'$ be a unital map of finite commutative rings killed by $N$, and let $B$ be a Noetherian scheme on which $N$ is invertible. Let $\pi:E\to B$ be a vector bundle of constant rank $r\geq0$ [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section]. Use ordinary small-etale derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], derived scalar tensor $Q_T=(-)\otimes_A^LA'$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], and the canonical proper/open compact-support scalar map $q_{f,M}:Q_YRf_{!,A}M\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{!,A'}Q_XM$ for compactifiable separated finite-type $f:X\to Y$ [lem-pur-etale-compact-scalar-coherence]. Let $u_T:Q_TA_T\xrightarrow{\sim}A'_T$ be multiplication, and let $l_{T,d}:Q_T(A_T(d)[2d])\xrightarrow{\sim}A'_T(d)[2d]$ be the normalized ordinary Tate balancing isomorphism of [lem-pur-finite-tate-scalar-source-normalization].

For $p:\mathbf P^1_B\to B$, put $W_R=R_{\mathbf P^1_B}(1)[2]$ for $R=A,A'$. Let $h_R:R_B\to Rp_{*,R}W_R$ be the scalar-extended Kummer class of $\mathcal O(1)$, and $b_R:R_B(1)[2]\oplus R_B\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_{*,R}W_R$ the decomposition with components the shifted twisted unit and $h_R$ [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction]. Define $\widetilde q_{p,W_A}=Rp_{*,A'}(l_{\mathbf P^1_B,1})q_{p,W_A}$, and let $d_B:Q_B(A_B(1)[2]\oplus A_B)\xrightarrow{\sim}A'_B(1)[2]\oplus A'_B$ have components $l_{B,1}$ and $u_B$. Then
$$\widetilde q_{p,W_A}Q_B(h_A)=h_{A'}u_B,\qquad \widetilde q_{p,W_A}Q_B(b_A)=b_{A'}d_B.$$
Consequently the actual projective-line traces $t_{p,R}=\operatorname{pr}_2b_R^{-1}$ [def-amb-p1-trace] satisfy
$$t_{p,A'}\widetilde q_{p,W_A}=u_BQ_B(t_{p,A}).$$
The affine-space coordinate-tower traces [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace] satisfy this same equation for every dimension $d\geq0$, using the specified compactification scalar comparison. For the global integrations [def-amb-vector-integration], put $W=A_E(r)[2r]$, $W'=A'_E(r)[2r]$ and $\widetilde q_{\pi,W}=R\pi_{!,A'}(l_{E,r})q_{\pi,W}$. Then
$$t_{\pi,A'}\widetilde q_{\pi,W}=u_BQ_B(t_{\pi,A}).$$
This is an equality of derived morphisms, with the actual open-restriction and compactification-refinement comparisons in $q$. It includes rank zero and the empty base. No flatness of $A'$ over $A$, assertion about scalar extension of individual cohomology groups, or general smooth-purity theorem is assumed.

source.place: paragraph 2, Kummer/projective-line coefficient reduction, affine-space composition and degree-zero bundle descent; old Steps 9--10

proof.text: Fix the normalized identifications throughout. The scalar functor is exact, and its tensor and composition comparisons are the K-flat comparisons. By the Tate normalization, $l_{T,0}=u_T$, $l_{T,1}$ is the balanced map, and $l_{T,d}$ is its tensor power with the prescribed shift. Thus the maps called $\theta^0,\theta^1[2]$ in the Kummer scalar lemma are precisely $u_T,l_{T,1}$ here: both send $(z\otimes a)\otimes b$ to $z\otimes\varphi(a)b$. The symmetric monoidal composition comparisons identify the two successive scalar extensions from $\mathbf Z/N$ with extension to $A'$; no ordinary tensor exactness along $A\to A'$ is being asserted. The Tate sheaves themselves are flat of rank one, so their derived extensions are the displayed shifted degree-zero sheaves. This also shows that every Tate input and its scalar extension used below is bounded below. The maps $l_{T,r}$ also commute with inverse image: for $f:X\to Y$, under the scalar/pullback comparison and the canonical Tate pullback identifications $f^{-1}A_Y(r)\cong A_X(r)$, $f^{-1}A'_Y(r)\cong A'_X(r)$ of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback], $f^*(l_{Y,r})$ equals $l_{X,r}$. Both sides are maps between shifted flat degree-zero sheaves, computed by the degree-zero resolutions; on such K-flat objects the scalar/pullback comparison is the ordinary module pullback of the tensor product [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], and the sheaf formula $(z\otimes a)\otimes b\mapsto z\otimes\varphi(a)b$ is preserved by inverse image of sections. Full faithfulness of the degree-zero embedding [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful] turns this equality of sheaf maps into the derived equality. This is the pullback compatibility of $l$ used in Steps 3, 5, 6 and 9.

source.place: paragraph 2, Kummer/projective-line coefficient reduction, affine-space composition and degree-zero bundle descent; old Steps 9--10

proof.text: Write $c_R:R_P\to W_R$ for the Kummer Chern morphism on $P=\mathbf P^1_B$. The Kummer scalar lemma, for the present arbitrary Noetherian base and integer $N$, gives $l_{P,1}Q_P(c_A)=c_{A'}u_P$. Its statement identifies the adjunct of $c_R$ with the specified $h_R$. For this proper map, $q_p$ is exactly the counit transpose of the proper coefficient-extension lemma. Consequently the adjunct of $q_{p,W_A}Q_B(h_A)$ is $Q_P(\varepsilon_{p,W_A})\lambda_p p_{A'}^*Q_B(h_A)=Q_P(\varepsilon_{p,W_A}p_A^*h_A)\lambda_{p,A_B}=Q_P(c_A)\lambda_{p,A_B}$. Here the middle equality is naturality of $\lambda_p$. Compose with $l_{P,1}$. The preceding Kummer equation and the normalized coefficient-unit comparison turn this adjunct into $c_{A'}p_{A'}^*(u_B)$, the adjunct of $h_{A'}u_B$. Injectivity of the inverse-image/direct-image adjunction bijection proves $\widetilde q_{p,W_A}Q_B(h_A)=h_{A'}u_B$.

source.place: paragraph 2, Kummer/projective-line coefficient reduction, affine-space composition and degree-zero bundle descent; old Steps 9--10

proof.text: Let $v_R:R_B(1)[2]\to Rp_{*,R}W_R$ be the first component of $b_R$, the twisted shifted adjunction unit. Put $L_R=R_B(1)[2]$, so that $p_R^*L_R=W_R$. The adjunct of $q_{p,W_A}Q_B(v_A)$ is $Q_P(\varepsilon_{p,W_A}p_A^*v_A)\lambda_{p,L_A}=\lambda_{p,L_A}$, because $\varepsilon_p p^*\eta_p=1$. Composing with $l_{P,1}$ gives $p_{A'}^*(l_{B,1})$ by the pullback compatibility of $l$ in Step 1 and the unit normalization of the Tate source node. This is the adjunct of $v_{A'}l_{B,1}$. Thus $\widetilde q_{p,W_A}Q_B(v_A)=v_{A'}l_{B,1}$. This calculation uses the specified unit and counit, rather than an unspecified isomorphism between the two decompositions.

source.place: paragraph 2, Kummer/projective-line coefficient reduction, affine-space composition and degree-zero bundle descent; old Steps 9--10

proof.text: Scalar tensor preserves the binary biproduct diagram. The preceding two component equations therefore give $\widetilde q_{p,W_A}Q_B(b_A)=b_{A'}d_B$. Postcompose with $t_{p,A'}=\operatorname{pr}_2b_{A'}^{-1}$: the result is $\operatorname{pr}_2d_B=u_BQ_B(\operatorname{pr}_2)$. Precompose with $Q_B(b_A^{-1})$ to obtain exactly $t_{p,A'}\widetilde q_{p,W_A}=u_BQ_B(t_{p,A})$. This argument does not split individual cohomology groups.

source.place: paragraph 2, Kummer/projective-line coefficient reduction, affine-space composition and degree-zero bundle descent; old Steps 9--10

proof.text:
For the standard open $j:\mathbf A^1_B\hookrightarrow P$, write $\beta_j:Q_Pj_{!,A}\cong j_{!,A'}Q_{\mathbf A^1}$ and $\lambda_j:j_{A'}^*Q_P\cong Q_{\mathbf A^1}j_A^*$. The open coefficient normalization says that $\beta_j^{-1}$ is the left mate of $\lambda_j^{-1}$. The mate-transpose formula, applied to the open counit $e_{A,M}:j_{!,A}j_A^*M\to M$ (whose transpose is the identity), gives
$$e_{A',Q_PM}\,j_{!,A'}(\lambda_{j,M}^{-1})\,\beta_{j,j_A^*M}=Q_P(e_{A,M}).$$
Take $M=W_A$ and follow with $l_{P,1}$. Naturality of the open counit and the Tate pullback identification give the same equation with $W_{A'}$ as target. The affine-line trace is $t_{p,R}\,Rp_{*,R}(e_{R,W_R})$, by its defining composite adjunction. Apply proper direct image to the open-counit equation and use naturality of the proper scalar map, followed by the projective-line trace equation of Step 4. Its composite is the affine-line trace equation. By the definition of compact-support scalar coherence, the coefficient map in this composite is exactly $q_{p_1}$ for this compactification.

source.place: paragraph 2, Kummer/projective-line coefficient reduction, affine-space composition and degree-zero bundle descent; old Steps 9--10

proof.text: We will also use the affine-line counit at a shifted Tate line $K=A_B(e)[2e]$. The projective-line adjunction specifies its counit as inverse projection followed by $1_K\otimes t_p$ and the unitor; composing with the open adjunction gives the same formula with $t_{p_1}$ and the proper/open projection map, whose open factor is the canonical isomorphism of [lem-pur-etale-open-derived-tensor]. Here naturality of the proper projection map in its second variable moves $1\otimes Rp_*(e_{W})$ past it, and the open tensor isomorphism followed by the open counit at $p^*K\otimes W$ is $1\otimes e_W$: on the degreewise sheaf identity of that node both maps are the identity over the open and zero off it. The projection square of compact-support scalar coherence identifies the scalar extension of this inverse projection with the primed inverse projection and $1\otimes q_{p_1}$. Its natural-isomorphism assertion permits inversion of the projection square (the projection in this counit formula is an isomorphism). Tensor the affine-line trace equation of Step 5 with $Q_BK$ and use the monoidal unit comparison. It follows that this entire counit commutes with scalar extension, with source map $a_{p_1,K}$ from the Tate normalization and target map $l_{B,e}$. All tensor reassociations and even shifts here are the fixed monoidal comparisons, not a new choice of trace.

source.place: paragraph 2, Kummer/projective-line coefficient reduction, affine-space composition and degree-zero bundle descent; old Steps 9--10

proof.text: Induct on $d$ simultaneously for every Noetherian base with $N$ invertible. Dimension zero is the identity adjunction, and dimension one is Step 5. Write $p_d=g f$, with $f:\mathbf A^d_B\to\mathbf A^{d-1}_B$ the last-coordinate line and $g=p_{d-1}$. By the definition of the ordered composite adjunction, its counit at the constant object is $t_{g,R}\,Rg_{!,R}(\epsilon_{f,R;K_R})$, where $K_R=R_{\mathbf A^{d-1}_B}(d-1)[2d-2]$; the right-functor identification makes the input $R_{\mathbf A^d_B}(d)[2d]$. Let $m_R=\epsilon_{f,R;K_R}$ and $W_{d,R}=R_{\mathbf A^d_B}(d)[2d]$. Step 6 says $m_{A'}Rf_{!,A'}(l_{\mathbf A^d,d})q_{f,W_{d,A}}=l_{\mathbf A^{d-1},d-1}Q(m_A)$. Under the compact-support composition comparison, scalar coherence writes $q_{gf}$ as $Rg_{!,A'}(q_f)q_g$. Substitute this factorization into $t_{g,A'}Rg_{!,A'}(m_{A'})q_{gf}$, including the line identification. Step 6 changes its inner factor to $Rg_{!,A'}(l\,Qm_A)q_g$. Naturality of $q_g$ moves $Qm_A$ to the right; the induction equation for $g$ changes the remaining left factor to $u_BQ(t_{g,A})$. The result is $u_BQ(t_{g,A}Rg_{!,A}(m_A))$, the required dimension-$d$ equation. These are the actual coordinate-tower counits of the top-trace node.

source.place: paragraph 2, Kummer/projective-line coefficient reduction, affine-space composition and degree-zero bundle descent; old Steps 9--10

proof.text: The composition and refinement clauses just used require bounded-below inputs both before and after scalar extension. They apply to $W_{d,A}$ and $W_{d,A'}$ by Step 1. For the outer comparison they also apply: the line counit at $K_A$ identifies $Rf_{!,A}W_{d,A}$ with $K_A$, and after scalar extension this is identified with the shifted flat line $K_{A'}$. All intermediate bases in the tower are finite type over $B$, hence Noetherian. Thus every induction application is within the hypotheses of the comparison nodes. Their refinement compatibility also shows that replacing the tower compactification by any proper refinement preserves the equation; it is an equation for the specified compact-support comparison.

source.place: paragraph 2, Kummer/projective-line coefficient reduction, affine-space composition and degree-zero bundle descent; old Steps 9--10

proof.text: Choose a Zariski open cover $v_i:U_i\hookrightarrow B$ trivializing $E$, with the same frames for both coefficient rings. Each $U_i$ and each overlap is Noetherian. By the definition of vector integration, $t_{\pi,R}|_{U_i}$ is precisely the affine-space trace after open compact-support exchange and the coordinate identification. The open-restriction square in compact-support scalar coherence, and the pullback compatibility of $l$, identify the restriction of $\widetilde q_{\pi,W}$ with the local scalar comparison. For the coordinate isomorphism, use the Cartesian square over $1_{U_i}$ identifying $E|_{U_i}$ with $\mathbf A^r_{U_i}$. Transport the chosen compactification along this isomorphism. The proper direct-image scalar-exchange equation and the open scalar-exchange equation identify its proper/open scalar map with the affine-space one. Proper-refinement coherence removes any choice of this transported compactification. Step 7 now proves the desired global equation after restriction to every $U_i$.

source.place: paragraph 2, Kummer/projective-line coefficient reduction, affine-space composition and degree-zero bundle descent; old Steps 9--10

proof.text: It remains to justify detection of equality, not just local isomorphy. Put $C_A=R\pi_{!,A}W$ and $C_{A'}=R\pi_{!,A'}W'$. The construction of vector integration gives $C_R\cong\mathcal H^0(C_R)[0]$ and a sheaf map defining $t_{\pi,R}$. Its restrictions are the affine-space trace isomorphisms. Thus its degree-zero sheaf map is invertible by cover detection, so $t_{\pi,R}$ is invertible. In particular $e=u_BQ_B(t_{\pi,A}):Q_BC_A\xrightarrow{\sim}A'_B[0]$ is invertible even for a nonflat coefficient map. The two morphisms in question have source $Q_BC_A$ and target $A'_B[0]$. Precompose both with $e^{-1}$; they are now endomorphisms of $A'_B[0]$ with equal restrictions by Step 9. Full faithfulness of the degree-zero embedding identifies them with two maps of module sheaves. Exact restriction of single complexes is compatible with this identification. Uniqueness of sheaf-Hom gluing makes the two sheaf maps equal, hence their derived morphisms equal. Cancel $e^{-1}$. This proves the asserted equality without any descent assertion for general derived morphisms.

source.place: paragraph 2, Kummer/projective-line coefficient reduction, affine-space composition and degree-zero bundle descent; old Steps 9--10

proof.text: For $r=0$, the affine-space adjunction and its trace are the identity; $l_{T,0}=u_T$ and the identity compact-support comparison has its unit normalization. The equation reduces to $u_B=u_B$. The rank-zero bundle has these same prescribed local identity traces, so Step 10 applies as well. If the base is empty, every module sheaf and every displayed complex is zero and every indicated morphism is the unique zero morphism. This includes $N=1$ (the coefficient rings are zero), and requires no positive-rank or nonempty-base assumption.
